Bench: Yogendra Kumar Purohit [2025:RJ-JD:30063]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Civil Transfer Appl. No. 62/2024 Smt. Monika Soni W/o Dr. Nishant Soni, Aged About 38 Years,
D/o Shri Daulatram Soni, R/o Nal Road, Near Dudi Petrol Pump And Bhram Sagar Shiv Mandir, Bangla Nagar, Bikaner.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
----Petitioner  Versus Dr. Nishant Soni S/o Nand Kishore Soni, Aged About 37 Years,
R/o 1/A/68, Kudi Bhagtasani Housing Board, Jodhpur.
----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. S.K.Verma  Mr. Mrinal Khatri For Respondent(s) : Mr. Vikram Singh Jaitawat  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGENDRA KUMAR PUROHIT Order 10/07/2025 1.

The petitioner-wife has filed the present civil transfer application seeking transfer of Case No.
1131/2023 (1135/2023) "Dr. Nishant Soni Vs. Smt. Monika Soni" preferred by the respondent-husband under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, pending before Family Court No.2, Jodhpur to the Family Court No.1, Bikaner.

entities.text: Dr. Nishant Soni Vs. Smt. Monika Soni
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the marriage between the parties was solemnized on 19.04.2022 as per Hindu rituals at Jodhpur.

However, since the petitioner-wife was harassed and abused for demand of dowry and for undergoing IVF for child birth, by the respondent-husband and his family members, therefore, fearing the safety of the petitioner, her parents brought the petitioner back to Bikaner.

Thereafter, numerous attempts were made for resolution of the dispute, [2025:RJ-JD:30063] (2 of 5) [CTA-62/2024] however, the in-laws persisted in their unlawful demands and subjected her to continuous harassment and abuse.

entities.text: Monika Soni vs Dr. Nishant Soni (2025:Rj-Jd:30063)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 with such situation, the petitioner submitted a written report against her husband and his family members, upon which, an FIR No. 307/2023 was registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, Bikaner for the offences under Section 498A, 323, 406 IPC.

She also filed two applications under Section 144 BNSS (125 Cr.P.C.) seeking maintenance and interim maintenance before Family Court No.1,
Bikaner.

However, with a view to harass and humiliate the petitioner, the respondent-husband has moved the application under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act seeking dissolution of marriage before Family Court No.1, Jodhpur and the same is pending at Family Court No.2, Jodhpur.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the petitioner is a lady and is presently residing with her parents at Bikaner.
The aforesaid cases filed by the petitioner-wife are pending at Bikaner.
Apart from this, the distance from Bikaner to Jodhpur is 239 kms. approx.
Neither the petitioner is having any independent source of income nor she is being paid any maintenance amount by the respondent-husband and is fully dependent upon her parents.

It is also submitted that the respondent is threatening the petitioner of dire consequences, therefore, she is afraid of happening of any untoward incident if she goes to Jodhpur to attend the court proceedings.

Thus, it is submitted that in the facts and circumstances of the case, it is very difficult, expensive and onerous for the petitioner to travel all alone to attend and defend the case filed by her husband at Jodhpur and in the interest of justice, since the cases filed by the petitioner-wife are pending at Bikaner, the case filed by the respondent-husband at Family Court, Jodhpur under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act deserves to be transferred to the Family Court No.1, Bikaner.
5.

A reply to the transfer application has been filed on behalf of the respondent-husband denying the averments made in the application and the allegations regarding dowry demand and pressurizing the petitioner to undergo IVF for child birth.

It is [2025:RJ-JD:30063] (3 of 5) [CTA-62/2024]
alleged that the petitioner misbehaved and used abusive language with the respondent and his family members and left her matrimonial home only after four days of the marriage and is residing at Bikaner.

Admitting the factum of lodging of the FIR by the petitioner, it is submitted that against the said FIR, the respondent preferred S.B.Criminal Misc. Petition No. 1354/2024 before this Court,
wherein, vide order dated 19.03.2024 an interim order has been passed by this Court in favour of the respondent.

It is stated that the respondent is doing private job at Abu Road and distance from Abu Road to Bikaner is 500 km. approx.
6.

Learned counsel appearing for the respondent-husband submitting the stand taken in the reply,
opposed the prayer for transfer of the case.
It is argued that mere inconvenience of the parties is not enough for seeking transfer of the case.

In this regard, learned counsel has relied upon a decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Dr. Subramaniam Swamy Vs. Ramakrishna Hedge,
reported in (1990) 1 SCC 4 as also a decision of the Hon'ble Karnataka High Court in the matter of Smt. H.K.Suma and Ors. Vs. M. Santosh, reported in (2022) 4 CivCC 773, wherein the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in Dr. Subramaniam Swamy (supra) was relied upon.

Dr. Subramaniam Swamy Vs. Ramakrishna Hedge,
reported in (1990) 1 SCC 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, learned counsel for the respondent prays for dismissal of the transfer petition.

7. From the perusal of the record, it is clear that the petitioner wife is residing at Bikaner with her parents and has filed the FIR against her husband and his family members as aforesaid in which matter is pending at Bikaner though on arrest there is an interim order passed by this Court.

As Smt. Monika Soni vs Dr. Nishant Soni (2025:Rj-Jd:30063) on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27165902/
2 stated by the counsel for the petitioner, the applications preferred by the petitioner under Section 144 BNSS seeking maintenance and interim maintenance, as aforesaid, are also pending consideration at Family Court No.1, Bikaner.

entities.text: Smt. Monika Soni vs Dr. Nishant Soni (2025:Rj-Jd:30063)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Regarding petitioner's financial capability also,
nothing
has been averred in the reply by the respondent.

8. It is settled law that while considering transfer of case in matrimonial proceedings instituted by the husband, the [2025:RJ-JD:30063] (4 of 5) [CTA-62/2024] convenience of the wife is to be looked into.

In this regard, recently, Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the matter of N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S.Saravana Karthik Sha, (Civil Appeal No.4894/2022 arising out of SLP (C) No.16465/2021)
decided on 18.7.2022, while considering transfer of matrimonial case under Section 24 CPC, has observed as under:-
"The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.

entities.text: N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S.Saravana Karthik Sha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance to life.
Given the prevailing socio-economic paradigm in the Indian society, generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer."

9. It is to be noticed that the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court relied upon by learned counsel for the respondent in the matter Dr. Subramaniam Swamy (supra) to strengthen his argument regarding inconvenience of the parties being not enough for transfer of the case, pertains to transfer of a civil suit not for matrimonial cases, and has been given in the facts and circumstances of that case.

Thereafter, Hon'ble Apex Court, recently while considering transfer of matrimonial case under Section 24 CPC, in the matter of N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S.Saravana Karthik Sha (supra) has held to generally look into the convenience of the wife while considering transfer.

entities.text: N.C.V. Aishwarya Vs. A.S.Saravana Karthik Sha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, the decisions cited by the learned counsel for the respondent are of no help to the respondent.

10. Having considered the submissions made on behalf of the parties, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case noticed above and the settled position of law by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of N.C.V. Aishwarya (supra), the transfer application is allowed.

It is ordered that Case No.1131/2023 [2025:RJ-JD:30063] (5 of 5) [CTA-62/2024] (1135/2023) "Dr. Nishant Soni Vs. Smt. Monika Soni" pending before Family Court No.2, Jodhpur be transferred to the Family Court No.1, Bikaner.

entities.text: Dr. Nishant Soni Vs. Smt. Monika Soni
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Family Court No.2, Jodhpur is directed to send the record of the aforesaid case to the Family Court No.1, Bikaner immediately.
The parties are directed to appear before the Family Court No.1, Bikaner on 07.8.2025.
A copy of this order be sent to the Family Court No.2, Jodhpur and Family Court No.1, Bikaner forthwith.
Stay application also stands disposed of.

(YOGENDRA KUMAR PUROHIT),J 69-RP/-
